decisions.reason: The GK 2.0 high-resolution printer is a flagship hardware generation that was promoted on the home page, carries heavy development investment and is central to REA JET's announced direction, so management will persist with it.

The numbering module was publicly announced in two languages as an expansion of the software portfolio, costs little to maintain and complements the printers, so there is little reason to withdraw it.

The coder for non-absorbent surfaces fills a core application niche in industrial coding, and having already invested in its ink and hardware, the firm will keep it and attribute any weak sales to temporary market conditions.
CodeScan was publicly positioned on its own page as the successor to PharmaScan, which commits the firm to it, though as a low-cost app it is somewhat more exposed to quiet replacement.
Inline code verification fits the firm's quality-assurance story and complements its printers, so sunk investment and strategic fit favour persistence.
The layout design software was featured on the home page and ties the firm's hardware ecosystem together, so management's visible commitment makes dropping it unlikely.
